Legal Standards.name: Endangered Species Act (ESA)
Legal Standards.note: The ESA provides for listing species and recovery obligations when populations are low (“threatened” or “endangered”). Once listed, it becomes illegal to take (harm) listed species and federal agencies must avoid actions that jeopardize them or destroy/modify their critical habitat. Agencies must develop recovery plans to increase population abundance.

key_elements.name: Listing and recovery planning
key_elements.note: Species with depressed abundance can be listed as threatened/endangered based on scientific status.

key_elements.name: Critical habitat protections
key_elements.note: Areas needed for recovery are defined and protected.

key_elements.name: Section 7 consultation
key_elements.note: Federal actions must consult with NOAA/FWS to avoid jeopardy to listed species.

Legal Standards.name: Magnus-Stevens Fishery Conservation and Management Act (MSA)
Legal Standards.note: MSA governs marine fisheries including salmon in federal waters and aims to prevent overfishing and rebuild overfished stocks. It requires fishery management plans (FMPs) with status determination criteria such as minimum stock levels and escapement goals to measure stock abundance.

key_elements.name: National standards
key_elements.note: Management actions must prevent overfishing and use the best scientific information.

key_elements.name: Essential Fish Habitat (EFH)
key_elements.note: Requires identification and protection of habitats necessary for salmon to spawn, feed, and mature.

Legal Standards.name: Pacific Coast Salmon Fishery Management Plan (PCSFMP)
Legal Standards.note: Under the MSA, the Pacific Fishery Management Council develops a detailed Salmon FMP that includes control rules, escapement benchmarks, and harvest limits tied explicitly to abundance metrics. These criteria determine allowable catch and management actions based on current and forecasted stock abundance.

Legal Standards.name: California State Law: AB 263 (2025)
Legal Standards.note: California law AB 263 extends emergency instream flow protections for key salmon tributaries (Scott & Shasta Rivers) to support salmon survival and spawning habitat, countering drought and water diversions that reduce abundance.

Legal Standards.name: Marine Life Protection Act (MLPA)
Legal Standards.note: State-level habitat protection through creation and evaluation of marine protected areas (MPAs) enhances ecosystem conditions beneficial to salmon nearshore life stages and contributes to abundance goals.

Governing Agencies.name: NOAA Fisheries (NMFS)
Governing Agencies.note: Implements ESA for marine salmon, approves FMPs under MSA, designates critical habitat, conducts consultations

Governing Agencies.name: Pacific Fishery Council
Governing Agencies.note: Develops the Salmon FMP, sets ACLs and escapement goals under MSA.

Governing Agencies.name: U.S. Fish & Wildlife Service
Governing Agencies.note: Shares ESA implementation for some salmon species.

Governing Agencies.name: California State Water Resources Control Board
Governing Agencies.note: Sets water flows and instream protections (e.g., AB 263).

Governing Agencies.name: California Dept. of Fish & Wildlife
Governing Agencies.note: Implements state harvest regulations and participates in habitat restoration.

Governing Agencies.name: Tribes
Governing Agencies.note: Have treaty water/fish rights and collaborate on salmon resotration (e.g., Klamath protections).
